subject: Post-call: NovaRetail deploy mode decision and dedicated capacity follow-ups
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@novaretail.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-01-19T16:05:00-08:00
Subject: Post-call: NovaRetail deploy mode decision and dedicated capacity follow-ups

Hi Emily,

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and the concrete asks we agreed on so we can get you a scoped POC and ballpark cost. Ive put the questions below to make the follow-up easier for your procurement and infra teams.

Recap from call
- Use cases: customer support triage + real-time product chat (about 10s latency target for chat).
- Expected peak traffic: 1,200 chat sessions per minute peak, average session length 120 tokens per message, and about 4 messages per session.
- Primary data residency: US-east.
- Security: SOC2 and customer-managed keys are required.
- Initial preference: leaning toward Dedicated capacity for predictable latency, but open to Hosted if we can meet encryption and SLA needs.

Follow-up items we need from you to finalize a POC scope
1) TPS / concurrency breakdown: for sizing we need sessions per second, average tokens per response, and percent of short vs long responses. For example, in our sizing worksheet a token mix of 70% 256-token responses and 30% 1024-token responses materially changes GPU selection.
2) Preferred GPU family: do you have procurement constraints or preferred GPU types (A100, H100, or Ampere/Tr4 equivalents on your side)? If not, we can recommend.
3) Minimum SLA targets for latency p95 and throughput.
4) Any strict egress / VPC peering windows or procurement timelines.

Actions we will take
- Attach a capacity worksheet for you to fill (attached). It has a sample token mix and asks for peak QPS, session concurrency, and latency SLO.
- Draft POC SOW and a high-level bill estimate for Dedicated capacity and a Hosted fallback option.

Please reply inline to the worksheet or send a quick message with the TPS and token mix. If easier, we can schedule a 30-minute call with your infra lead later this week.

Best,
Soojin
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: novaretail_capacity_sheet_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet), redwood_poc_scope_and_estimate.pdf (PDF)

From: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@novaretail.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-01-20T08:14:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: NovaRetail deploy mode decision and dedicated capacity follow-ups

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the clear recap. Ive filled the high level numbers below; Ill loop procurement this morning for the detailed worksheet fill.

High-level answers
- Peak sessions per minute: 1,200 (as discussed). Thats ~20 sessions per second.
- Average messages per session: 4 (2 user messages, 2 assistant responses on average).
- Typical response token length: 60 tokens for short responses, 600 tokens for detailed responses. Estimated mix: 65% short, 35% long.
- Expected concurrency: at peak, about 800 concurrent active sessions.
- Preferred GPU: procurement prefers H100 if cost delta is acceptable, but we are open to alternatives.
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 250 ms for short responses, p95 <= 800 ms for long responses.
- Data residency: must be US-east; we need KMS integration.

Procurement will likely ask for a cost table and a sample SOW. Can you include a Hosted-vs-Dedicated comparison in the estimates, so I can present options to our CFO?

Emily
VP, Product
NovaRetail

Emily,

Appreciate the numbers these are super helpful. A couple clarifying q's before we size and propose a POC: 

1) Token mix detail: when you say 65% short (60 tokens) and 35% long (600 tokens), is that measured per assistant response or per full turn? We assume per assistant response.

2) Concurrency: you mentioned 800 concurrent active sessions at peak. Is that simultaneous active websocket connections or sessions with cached KV state? That impacts how we provision KV cache and memory per-worker.

3) H100 preference: happy to size H100-based configurations but will surface the cost delta to A100 for comparison. Do you want us to include a quantized 4-bit option to show cost tradeoffs?

Next steps
- Marcus will run a quick sizing run and share two options: H100 dedicated pool estimate and an H100-hosted hybrid option (hosted for burst, dedicated for baseline).
- Ill also prepare a short 1-page comparison table for CFO highlighting predictable monthly commit vs on-demand hosted uplift.

Can you confirm the concurrency semantics and whether KMS is customer-managed with AWS KMS key alias? That will help for the Private/VPC checklist too.

Thanks,
Soojin

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-01-21T09:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: NovaRetail deploy mode decision and dedicated capacity follow-ups

Emily,

Quick sizing note based on the numbers Soojin captured:
- Peak assistant responses per second estimate: (20 sessions/s) x (2 assistant responses per session) = 40 responses/s.
- Token throughput at peak with your mix:
  - Short responses: 65% of 40 = 26 responses/s x 60 tokens = 1560 tokens/s
  - Long responses: 35% of 40 = 14 responses/s x 600 tokens = 8400 tokens/s
  - Total tokens/s = 9960 tokens/s (~9.96k tokens/s)

Sizing implications (ballpark)
- H100 baseline: 1 x H100 per 40 concurrent generation workers (depending on model family and quantization). For your token mix we recommend an H100-dedicated pool of 4 GPUs to meet bursty long-response demand with autoscaling to 6 for peaks.
- A100 alternative: 1 x A100 per 25 workers, so you would need ~6 A100s baseline to match baseline throughput. Cost delta is material.
- Hybrid option: Dedicated 3 H100s for baseline + Hosted burst capacity for peak windows reduces committed cost by ~25% but adds hosted egress considerations.

Next steps I propose
- If NovaRetail can confirm that the 800 concurrent sessions are active websocket connections, we should add an extra H100 for memory/KV headroom.
- I will attach a quick raw sizing table. Once procurement confirms KMS and procurement timelines we can finalize an SOW.

Ill drop the sizing workbook in the shared Drive folder and loop in Solutions Engineering for a short review call.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
